title: sysc-wayland v0.2.0: unknown surface enter is fatal
description:
Reproduced live 2026-08-31 on the laptop. Opening the system-monitor panel kills the shell on the first toggle: 'dispatch: panic handling opcode=0 senderID=19: client: invalid server object ID 0x20'. senderID 19 is the wl_pointer; opcode 0 is wl_pointer.enter. The object id varies per run (0x185, 0x20), always client-range.

Cause is in the pinned dependency, not the shell. client/client.go Pointer.Dispatch case 0: if GetProxy(surfaceID) misses or the surface is a zombie, it does 'surface := &Surface{}; RegisterWithID(surface, surfaceID)'. RegisterWithID panics when id < firstServerID (0xff000000), so any enter naming a client-created surface the client has destroyed is fatal. The same generated fallback appears for keyboard enter/leave and other object-typed event arguments (client.go 2740, 2759, 2772, 2817, 4527, 4544, 5578, 5601, 6069); the scanner emits RegisterWithID for every object argument, conflating an existing-object reference with a new_id.

Correct behavior: an enter naming an unknown or zombie surface leaves e.Surface nil and the event is ignored. Never register a client-range id.

Consequence here: destroying any aux surface races a queued enter. sysc-shell can shrink the window but cannot close it. The teardown ordering fix in c7bcc7c is still correct and still insufficient. This is the true cause of sysc-42, and it blocks the M4 live gate. M5 makes it worse: toasts, tray menus and the notification centre add many short-lived surfaces under the pointer.

Needs a sysc-wayland fix and a new tag; sysc-shell then repins.
notes: Rechecked 2026-09-01: sysc-shell pins v0.2.0, whose generated Pointer.Dispatch and Keyboard.Dispatch still call RegisterWithID for unknown nonzero surface IDs. The upstream fix and a later pinned tag remain required.

title: Battery icon font: all seven level glyphs are identical
description:
internal/render/icons/sysc-icons.ttf draws codepoints 0xE008 to 0xE00E (battery levels 0..6) as the same solid silhouette. Rendering the band at 96pt and at the bar's 17px shows no difference between an empty and a full battery.

BatteryIconRune is correct: 73 percent maps to level 5 of 0..6 and iconfont_test asserts every charge lands in the band. The selection works and the asset does not encode what was selected, so a battery widget cannot communicate charge through its icon. Live at 73 percent it reads as a solid block.

Fix belongs in the font asset: seven discharging and seven charging glyphs that actually differ, ideally an outline with a partial fill so the level reads at 17px. Check the critical glyph too. A test that rasterises each level and asserts the glyphs differ would stop this recurring, since the existing test only checks codepoint mapping.

Discovered live 2026-08-31 alongside sysc-43.

title: Group the sysmon widgets in one holder pill
description:
Live review 2026-08-31: cpu and memory each getting their own capsule reads as loose numbers. Owner wants them grouped; battery stays separate in its own pill.

The references disagree, so this is an owner decision, not a correction. DMS gives every status widget its own capsule. Noctalia runs the sysmon cluster as one continuous group with no inner pills.

Decision: one holder pill containing flat icon and value runs. Do not nest pills inside pills. The workspace row is already a pill row inside a capsule and reads as one indistinct blob in the live capture, our capsule contrast is 1.08 to 1 so two nested surfaces cannot be told apart, and Noctalia, the grouped reference, is flat inside.

Blocker: grouping is not expressible. Bar.Left, Center and Right are flat Item slices. Add an explicit group item carrying nested items, built as one capsule wrapping a KindRow. The layout machinery already exists from the parity tranche: capsuled wraps anything, measureNode sizes a row inside a capsule, and placeSection arranges capsule contents.

Sequence after sysc-53: a group of bare numbers is barely better than two pills of bare numbers, so the icons are what make a grouped cluster legible.

title: Group members are not centred inside their capsule
description:
Live 2026-08-31: the grouped cpu and memory values sit off-centre inside the group pill.

Introduced by the group tranche. measureNode for KindRow now reports the tallest child rather than the band it was offered, so text measured at the physical size is not cropped. layoutCapsuleChild then grows the layout box to that height when it exceeds the capsule's inner band. Layout centres children against content.H of the grown box, not against the visible capsule, so members are pushed off centre.

Fix: centre members against the capsule's own inner band while still measuring them at their natural height. Add a test asserting a member's vertical centre matches the capsule's, with a child taller than the offered band.

title: Bar status widgets have no tooltips
description:
Live 2026-08-31: grouped metrics render as bare percentages, so it is not possible to tell which value is cpu and which is memory. Grouping made this worse by removing the separation that hinted at distinct widgets.

textWidget already carries a tooltip field and the weather widget sets one; the metric, battery and workspace widgets do not. The dwell controller and tooltip surface exist from Tranche 3D, so this is populating a field and naming each metric, not new machinery.

Note sysc-32, sysc-33 and sysc-34 are open defects against that tooltip path: buffers are not retired on release, the surface ignores the accepted theme and font, and a cancelled dwell can still show. Fix those first or this widens their exposure.

title: Bar renders corrupt output on the laptop; cause not established
description:
2026-09-01. The bar paints scattered coloured blocks instead of content, or is absent and the window behind shows through. Process alive, single instance, log completely silent.

Not reproduced in tests. The same commit and the same font rendered correctly earlier in the same session, so the variable is not obviously the code.

Ruled out by reverting one at a time, none of which restored it: icon advance width 1260 back to 900, usWinAscent 1100 back to 900, and the entire internal/render/icons directory back to the prior commit. Also checked: only one sysc-shell process, no competing shell running.

Untested hypothesis: session state after roughly a dozen kill and restart cycles, which is the territory of sysc-51. A Niri session restart would rule that in or out and was not tried. The pre-session binary is kept at ~/.local/bin/sysc-shell.pre-fix.

Establish the cause before trusting any further live capture from that machine, since a bad session invalidates visual judgement of every other issue.

title: Registry audio/brightness OSD relay races with service swap
description:
go test -race ./internal/shell fails on main at 2c2fb7e (~20 tests in one package; the non-race run is clean).

Root cause: Registry.setAudio writes r.audio then launches 'go r.relayAudioOSD()', and the goroutine reads r.audio with no synchronisation. A second setAudio (service reload, or a test that swaps the service) writes the field while a live relay goroutine reads it. registry.go:102 (write) vs registry.go:271 (read). setBrightness has the same shape.

Found during Milestone 6A Task 0 reconciliation. Pre-existing, not caused by M6. Recorded rather than fixed because Registry is being changed by the in-flight M5 work.

Fix direction: pass the service to relayAudioOSD as an argument, or guard the field under the existing Registry mutex, and give the relay goroutine a per-generation stop signal so an old relay cannot outlive its service.
